story.text: "John Dewey (/ˈduːi/; October 20, 1859 – June 1, 1952) was an American philosopher, psychologist, and educational reformer."

Probably got to know about Dewey via my interest in education, particularly reflective practice. My first reference in my citation database is in 2018 ("How we think"), though I think my interest reaches back longer.
My favorite paper of him is probably [https://brocku.ca/MeadProject/Dewey/Dewey_1896.html "The Reflex Arc Concept in Psychology"]

It picks up a lot of characteristic ideas that stay with Dewey until his death: The close observation of everday activities, the importance of the material world without avoiding interiority, intentionality and learning. Typically, Dewey redefines terms rather than introducing new terms or latinisms and he assumes a unity of experience that he analyzes into different aspects (doing/undergoing, sensoric/motoric...) without assuming that the split is underlying – its an help in thinking, not revealing what the world actually is.
[[Susan Leigh Star]] Pragmatist, alluding in her first book to "the quest for certainty"
[[Donald Schön]] uses Deweys ideas to analyze moves and reflection in action.
[[Everyday]] situations were interesting for Dewey; in turn he appreciated abstractions but was concerns about ideas of their universal application.
